title: How early detection could change autism diagnosis and intervention, with Geraldine Dawson, PhD

sentences.en: Before we get started today, I'd like to ask you, our listeners, to take a moment to fill out our listener survey.
sentences.zh: 在今天节目开始之前，我想请各位听众花点时间填写一下我们的听众调查问卷。

sentences.en: We want to learn more about what you think of this podcast, who you are, and what you'd like to hear from us.
sentences.zh: 我们想更多地了解您对本播客的看法、您的身份，以及您希望从我们这里听到什么内容。

sentences.en: So if you could, after you listen to this episode, please go to our website at www.speakingofpsychology.org and look for the link to the listener survey.
sentences.zh: 如果您方便的话，请在听完这期节目后，访问我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org，找到听众调查问卷的链接。

sentences.en: We'd really appreciate it if you would take it.
sentences.zh: 如果您能参与填写，我们将不胜感激。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Now on to the episode.
sentences.zh: 现在进入本期节目。

sentences.en: About 1 in 36 children in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 根据美国疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）的最新估算，

sentences.en: has been diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder, according to the most recent Centers for Disease Control estimates.
sentences.zh: 美国约有 1/36 的儿童被诊断出患有自闭症谱系障碍。

sentences.en: Many of those children are not diagnosed until they're 3 to 5 years old, and some even later than that.
sentences.zh: 许多孩子直到 3 到 5 岁才被确诊，有些甚至更晚。

sentences.en: Scientists used to think that it was not possible to diagnose autism at a much younger age, but recent research using artificial intelligence, brain biomarkers, and other methods
sentences.zh: 科学家过去认为在更小的年龄诊断自闭症是不可能的，但最近利用人工智能、大脑生物标志物和其他方法的研究

sentences.en: has pointed to the possibility of earlier detection and earlier intervention.
sentences.zh: 指出了实现更早发现和更早干预的可能性。

sentences.en: Today, we'll talk about research on autism, autism diagnosis, and interventions.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将讨论关于自闭症、自闭症诊断以及干预措施的研究。

sentences.en: Why has the number of diagnoses risen so steeply in recent years?
sentences.zh: 为什么近年来确诊人数急剧上升？

sentences.en: Why is autism so much more common in boys than in girls?
sentences.zh: 为什么自闭症在男孩中比在女孩中常见得多？

sentences.en: And how might these new technologies and methods change autism detection and intervention?
sentences.zh: 这些新技术和新方法又将如何改变自闭症的检测和干预？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人 Kim Mills。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Geraldine Dawson, the William Cleland Distinguished Professor of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences at Duke University.
sentences.zh: 今天我的嘉宾是杜克大学精神病学与行为科学系的 William Cleland 特聘教授 Geraldine Dawson 博士。

sentences.en: She is also director of the Duke Center for Autism and Brain Development.
sentences.zh: 她同时担任杜克大学自闭症与大脑发育中心主任。

sentences.en: Dr. Dawson's work focuses on improving methods for early detection and intervention for autism and understanding brain function in autism.
sentences.zh: Dawson 博士的工作重点是改进自闭症的早期检测和干预方法，并理解自闭症患者的大脑功能。

sentences.en: Earlier in her career, she co-developed the Early Start Denver model, an empirically validated early autism intervention that is used worldwide.
sentences.zh: 在职业生涯早期，她共同开发了“丹佛早期启动模式”（Early Start Denver Model），这是一种在全球范围内得到实证验证的自闭症早期干预方法。

sentences.en: She collaborates with colleagues in the departments of computer science and engineering, pediatrics, and biostatistics to develop novel digital health approaches
sentences.zh: 她与计算机科学与工程系、儿科系以及生物统计学系的同事合作，开发创新的数字健康方法，

sentences.en: to autism screening and outcome monitoring.
sentences.zh: 用于自闭症筛查和结果监测。

sentences.en: Dr. Dawson has won many awards for her work, including a Distinguished Career Award from APA's Society of Clinical Child and Adolescent Psychology.
sentences.zh: Dawson 博士因其工作获得了许多奖项，包括美国心理学会临床儿童与青少年心理学分会颁发的杰出职业生涯奖。

sentences.en: Dr. Dawson, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: Dawson 博士，感谢您今天接受我的采访。

sentences.en: I'm very happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: Can you start by just giving us some background on what autism spectrum disorder is and encompasses?
sentences.zh: 您能先为我们介绍一下什么是自闭症谱系障碍，它涵盖了哪些方面吗？

sentences.en: Because it can look very different in different people.
sentences.zh: 因为在不同人身上，它的表现可能非常不同。

sentences.en: Is that correct?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yes, you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 是的，您说得完全正确。

sentences.en: In fact, there's a saying that says, if you've met one person with autism, you've met one person with autism.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有句名言说：如果你见过一个自闭症患者，那你也就只见过这一个自闭症患者。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that it is a very heterogeneous condition.
sentences.zh: 原因在于这是一种非常异质性的疾病。

sentences.en: So, for example, about 30% of people on the autism spectrum never learn to speak.
sentences.zh: 例如，约 30% 的自闭症谱系人士终生无法学会说话。

sentences.en: Many may require 24-7 care to help them with their very basic needs.
sentences.zh: 许多人可能需要全天候的照护来帮助他们处理最基本的生活需求。

sentences.en: And at the other end of the continuum, there are individuals who are highly intelligent.
sentences.zh: 而在谱系的另一端，也有一些智力水平很高的人。

sentences.en: We have an autistic researcher here at the center who has a PhD in physics.
sentences.zh: 我们中心就有一位患有自闭症的研究员，他拥有物理学博士学位。

sentences.en: So, there's just this huge continuum.
sentences.zh: 所以，这中间存在着一个巨大的连续谱。

sentences.en: So, that does beg the question then, you know, what is autism?
sentences.zh: 那么，这确实引出了一个问题：到底什么是自闭症？

sentences.en: What brings all of this together?
sentences.zh: 是什么将所有这些表现联系在一起的呢？

sentences.en: And in every case, the individual has some challenges in navigating the social world,
sentences.zh: 在每一个病例中，患者在应对社交世界时都会遇到一些挑战，

sentences.en: may have some difficulty in picking up on social cues and interpreting sort of the normal type of social information, such as gestures, facial expressions.
sentences.zh: 可能在捕捉社交线索和解读常规社交信息（如手势、面部表情）方面存在困难。

sentences.en: That individual also may have trouble forming social relationships.
sentences.zh: 患者在建立社交关系方面也可能遇到困难。

sentences.en: So, for example, developing peer relationships and just understanding sort of the back and forth reciprocal nature of relationships.
sentences.zh: 例如，在发展同伴关系以及理解社交互动中那种“你来我往”的互惠本质方面存在障碍。

sentences.en: And then there's also another category of behaviors which have to do with the tendency to engage in what we call a restricted range of interests or behaviors.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有另一类行为，即倾向于从事我们所说的“受限的兴趣或行为”。

sentences.en: So, that individual may be highly interested in one topic and want to talk about that topic and spend most of the time thinking about that topic.
sentences.zh: 患者可能对某个特定主题非常感兴趣，只想谈论该主题，并将大部分时间花在思考该主题上。

sentences.en: May also show some repetitive motor behaviors.
sentences.zh: 也可能表现出一些重复性的动作行为。

sentences.en: And then finally, with the DSM-5, an additional trait was added, and that is differences in sensory sensitivity.
sentences.zh: 最后，在《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》第 5 版（DSM-5）中，增加了一个额外的特征，即感官敏感性的差异。

sentences.en: So, it may be sensitivity to sound or to light or to touch.
sentences.zh: 比如，可能对声音、光线或触觉敏感。

sentences.en: And so, all of these things together comprise what we call the autism syndrome.
sentences.zh: 所有这些因素共同构成了我们所说的自闭症综合征。

sentences.en: And then, you know, this may be manifest in very different ways depending on each individual.
sentences.zh: 而且，根据每个人的不同，这些表现方式也会大相径庭。

sentences.en: Now, some of our listeners might be familiar with the term Asperger's syndrome, but that term isn't used now.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们的一些听众可能熟悉“阿斯伯格综合征”这个词，但这个词现在已经不再使用了。

sentences.en: Can you explain why that's fallen out of favor?
sentences.zh: 您能解释一下为什么它不再被采用了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so Asperger's syndrome was defined as having difficulties in the areas of social interaction and communication,
sentences.zh: 好的，阿斯伯格综合征曾被定义为在社交互动和沟通方面存在困难，

sentences.en: as well as those restricted and repetitive behaviors, but not having intellectual disability or language delay.
sentences.zh: 同时伴有那些受限和重复的行为，但没有智力障碍或语言发育迟缓。

sentences.en: And so, that sort of begged the question of how is that different than just an individual on the autism spectrum, you know, who doesn't have intellectual disability.
sentences.zh: 这引发了一个问题：这与那些没有智力障碍的自闭症谱系人士有什么区别呢？

sentences.en: So, you know, there were many studies that tried to disentangle those two ways of thinking about people on the highest end of the spectrum.
sentences.zh: 因此，有许多研究试图理清这两种看待谱系高端人群的方式。

sentences.en: And we really couldn't define any differences.
sentences.zh: 但我们实际上无法定义出任何区别。

sentences.en: The other thing is that clinicians were very unreliable in diagnosing, you know, autism without intellectual disability versus Asperger's syndrome.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，临床医生在区分“无智力障碍的自闭症”和“阿斯伯格综合征”时非常不一致。

sentences.en: And then finally, since many individuals are not diagnosed until later in life, it required the individual to base their symptom or their behavior on history, right?
sentences.zh: 最后，由于许多人直到成年后才被诊断，这要求患者根据病史来判断症状或行为，对吧？

sentences.en: You would have to ask the individual when you were a child, did you have any difficulty developing language?
sentences.zh: 你必须问患者：你小时候在语言发展方面是否有过困难？

sentences.en: And that was simply unreliable.
sentences.zh: 而这根本不可靠。

sentences.en: People couldn't really remember, you know, what their language history was many years later.
sentences.zh: 人们在多年后很难准确回忆起自己的语言发育史。

sentences.en: So, for all those reasons, the DSM committee, and by the way, that's the American Psychiatric Association Committee that comes up with the diagnostic criteria.
sentences.zh: 因此，出于所有这些原因，DSM 委员会（顺便提一下，这是美国精神医学学会负责制定诊断标准的委员会），

sentences.en: They decided that it was best to go ahead and eliminate that and think of autism as just a spectrum.
sentences.zh: 他们决定最好还是取消这个分类，将自闭症视为一个统一的谱系。

sentences.en: And then some individuals also have intellectual disability and language delay.
sentences.zh: 当然，有些人确实伴有智力障碍和语言发育迟缓。

sentences.en: And I think that change has been good.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种改变是好的。

sentences.en: It did create some, I think, challenges for people who really identified with being, having the diagnosis of Asperger's syndrome,
sentences.zh: 它确实给那些真正认同自己患有“阿斯伯格综合征”的人带来了一些挑战，

sentences.en: you know, so-called Asperger's syndrome, or there were a lot of groups that came together to socialize that were diagnosed with Asperger's syndrome.
sentences.zh: 或者说，有很多为了社交而聚集在一起的群体，他们都被诊断为阿斯伯格综合征。

sentences.en: And so, there was a point made that people could certainly continue to consider that, you know, as a personal way of describing themselves or personal identity.
sentences.zh: 因此，有人提出，人们当然可以继续将其作为一种描述自己的个人方式或个人身份认同。

sentences.en: It just wasn't going to be recognized anymore by the, according to the American Psychiatric Association's diagnostic criteria.
sentences.zh: 只是它不再被美国精神医学学会的诊断标准所认可了。

sentences.en: Well, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有道理。

sentences.en: Well, let me ask you what we know about the causes of autism.
sentences.zh: 那么，请问我们对自闭症的成因了解多少？

sentences.en: Is it genetic?
sentences.zh: 是遗传的吗？

sentences.en: Is it caused by something that happened to the mother during pregnancy or something else?
sentences.zh: 还是由母亲在怀孕期间发生的事情或其他因素引起的？

sentences.en: So, the causes of autism are complex.
sentences.zh: 自闭症的成因很复杂。

sentences.en: I think it's, first, it's important to keep in mind that autism is a condition that is a difference in the way the brain develops.
sentences.zh: 我认为首先要记住的是，自闭症是一种大脑发育方式上的差异。

sentences.en: And so, just as in neurotypical individuals, there are many factors that contribute to how, you know, each of us has a different brain in terms of its capabilities, its strengths,
sentences.zh: 就像神经典型个体一样，有许多因素影响着我们每个人的大脑在能力、优势、

sentences.en: its weaknesses, and how it develops.
sentences.zh: 弱点以及发育方式上的不同。

sentences.en: And that includes both genetic factors.
sentences.zh: 这既包括遗传因素。

sentences.en: So, autism is a highly genetic condition.
sentences.zh: 自闭症是一种高度遗传的疾病。

sentences.en: It can run in families.
sentences.zh: 它具有家族聚集性。

sentences.en: And you do see, you know, families with multiple children with a diagnosis of autism.
sentences.zh: 你确实会看到有多个孩子被诊断出患有自闭症的家庭。

sentences.en: Interestingly, it also runs in families with other conditions such as ADHD.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，它也常与多动症（ADHD）等其他疾病在同一家族中出现。

sentences.en: So, there seems to be some overlap, genetically, between autism and ADHD.
sentences.zh: 因此，自闭症和多动症之间似乎存在某种遗传上的重叠。

sentences.en: So, genetic factors are clearly contributing.
sentences.zh: 所以，遗传因素显然在起作用。

sentences.en: And they are contributing in such a way that the brain is developing differently, we know, starting in the prenatal period.
sentences.zh: 而且它们的作用方式导致了大脑从产前阶段就开始出现不同的发育。

sentences.en: And we also know that during the prenatal period,
sentences.zh: 我们也知道，在产前阶段，

sentences.en: anything that is going to affect the mother that also affects the brain of the baby that's developing could contribute to differences in brain development and also could,
sentences.zh: 任何影响母亲并进而影响胎儿大脑发育的因素，都可能导致大脑发育的差异，

sentences.en: in that sense, contribute to autism.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，也可能导致自闭症。

sentences.en: So, for example, one of the theories that is being investigated is what's called the maternal immune activation hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 例如，目前正在研究的理论之一是所谓的“母体免疫激活假说”。

sentences.en: And what that is, is a hypothesis that environmental conditions that activate the mother's immune system will influence the way that the fetal brain is developing.
sentences.zh: 该假说认为，激活母亲免疫系统的环境条件会影响胎儿大脑的发育方式。

sentences.en: It used to be thought that the brain of the fetus was entirely protected from these environmental conditions that the mother may be experiencing that affected her immune system.
sentences.zh: 过去人们认为，胎儿的大脑完全不受母亲所经历的那些影响其免疫系统的环境条件的干扰。

sentences.en: But now we know that, actually, anything that is activating her immune system during pregnancy could potentially affect, you know, aspects of the brain development,
sentences.zh: 但现在我们知道，实际上，任何在怀孕期间激活母亲免疫系统的因素，都可能影响大脑发育的某些方面，

sentences.en: particularly cells that are called the microglia,
sentences.zh: 特别是被称为“小胶质细胞”的细胞，

sentences.en: which are immune-related cells in the brain that actually participate in the development of synapses and the formation of the brain.
sentences.zh: 它们是大脑中与免疫相关的细胞，实际上参与了突触的发育和大脑的形成。

sentences.en: So, what can affect the mother's immune system during pregnancy?
sentences.zh: 那么，怀孕期间什么会影响母亲的免疫系统呢？

sentences.en: Really, really, really, really, really a wide range of conditions.
sentences.zh: 范围非常、非常、非常广泛。

sentences.en: So, for example, stress, you know, activates our immune system.
sentences.zh: 例如，压力会激活我们的免疫系统。

sentences.en: Environmental factors such as toxins, so pesticides or air traffic pollution can activate our immune system.
sentences.zh: 环境因素，如毒素（杀虫剂或交通废气污染），也会激活我们的免疫系统。

sentences.en: Having a significant infectious disease associated with high fever will obviously affect your immune system.
sentences.zh: 患有伴随高烧的严重传染病显然会影响免疫系统。

sentences.en: And, in fact, there's been studies now looking at, you know, the impact of having COVID-19 during pregnancy on, you know,
sentences.zh: 事实上，现在已经有研究在观察怀孕期间感染 COVID-19 对

sentences.en: the neurodevelopmental outcomes of the baby and there can be an impact.
sentences.zh: 婴儿神经发育结果的影响，确实可能会产生影响。

sentences.en: So, we believe that it is this combination of both genetic susceptibilities with environmental factors, particularly those that affect the mother during pregnancies,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们认为正是遗传易感性与环境因素（特别是那些在怀孕期间影响母亲的因素）的结合，

sentences.en: that are shaping all of our brains, right?
sentences.zh: 塑造了我们所有人的大脑，对吧？

sentences.en: Not just in autism, but also are contributing to differences that we then ultimately would diagnose as autism.
sentences.zh: 这不仅适用于自闭症，也导致了我们最终诊断为自闭症的那些差异。

sentences.en: So, I mentioned in my introduction the prevalence of ASD is much higher among boys than it is among girls, four times higher, in fact.
sentences.zh: 我在介绍中提到，自闭症谱系障碍在男孩中的患病率远高于女孩，事实上高出四倍。

sentences.en: Do researchers know why?
sentences.zh: 研究人员知道原因吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it's been an amazing kind of phenomenon to watch the prevalence of autism increasing over the last several decades.
sentences.zh: 是的，过去几十年来，观察自闭症患病率的上升是一个令人惊叹的现象。

sentences.en: I've been in the field for many decades now.
sentences.zh: 我从事这个领域已经几十年了。

sentences.en: And when I first started as a psychologist, I thought I would be this expert in helping individuals with this very rare condition.
sentences.zh: 当我刚开始做心理学家时，我以为我会成为帮助这种罕见疾病患者的专家。

sentences.en: And I imagined sort of myself, I was in the Northwest then, as being kind of the person that might serve people in the Northwest or the Western part of the United States.
sentences.zh: 当时我在西北部，我设想自己会成为服务于美国西北部或西部地区的人。

sentences.en: And now, of course, you know, autism spectrum disorder is really relatively common.
sentences.zh: 而现在，当然，自闭症谱系障碍已经相当普遍了。

sentences.en: And to be truthful, we don't completely understand, you know, even the epidemiologists and experts in the area of, you know, understanding differences in prevalence and so forth,
sentences.zh: 老实说，我们并不完全了解，即使是流行病学家和该领域的专家，

sentences.en: like people at the CDC.
sentences.zh: 比如 CDC 的那些人，

sentences.en: They don't fully understand why there's been an increase.
sentences.zh: 他们也并不完全了解为什么患病率会有所上升。

sentences.en: But when we do study it,
sentences.zh: 但当我们进行研究时，

sentences.en: what we find is there really has been changes in both the diagnostic criteria where they've now broadened somewhat from where the criteria that we had early on.
sentences.zh: 我们发现诊断标准确实发生了变化，与我们早期的标准相比，现在的范围有所扩大。

sentences.en: And then secondly, we're just so much better at recognizing autism.
sentences.zh: 其次，我们现在识别自闭症的能力强多了。

sentences.en: And you probably yourself, you know, now, you know, can recognize autism, whereas, you know, 30 years ago, you probably couldn't.
sentences.zh: 你可能自己现在也能识别出自闭症，而 30 年前你可能做不到。

sentences.en: So I think that we're now able to diagnose autism with individuals who have milder traits and also at a much earlier age.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，我们现在能够诊断出那些症状较轻的个体，并且诊断年龄也大大提前了。

sentences.en: And, you know, keep in mind that these prevalence estimates are really based on just looking at how many times a person is,
sentences.zh: 请记住，这些患病率估算实际上只是基于观察在特定地理区域内有多少人

sentences.en: how many people are diagnosed in a particular geographic area.
sentences.zh: 被诊断出来。

sentences.en: And so if you see, you know, if we're getting better at early detection, we're going to see these prevalence rates go up.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们能更好地进行早期检测，患病率数据自然会上升。

sentences.en: But we don't know whether there might have been, say, environmental factors that also could have contributed to the increase.
sentences.zh: 但我们不知道是否还有其他环境因素也促成了这种增长。

sentences.en: And it's also hard to know because the diagnostic criteria have changed over time.
sentences.zh: 而且很难判断，因为诊断标准随着时间的推移而发生了变化。

sentences.en: So what you're measuring is changing.
sentences.zh: 所以你测量的内容本身就在变化。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that just makes it very hard to know.
sentences.zh: 这使得情况变得非常复杂。

sentences.en: Well, a lot of your work has focused on early detection and intervention.
sentences.zh: 您的许多工作都集中在早期检测和干预上。

sentences.en: What does early mean for an autism diagnosis?
sentences.zh: 对于自闭症诊断来说，“早期”意味着什么？

sentences.en: At what age is it typically diagnosed?
sentences.zh: 通常在什么年龄确诊？

sentences.en: Well, let's start with when it can be reliably diagnosed.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们先从什么时候可以可靠地诊断开始说起。

sentences.en: So we know that we can reliably diagnose autism by 18 to 24 months, certainly by 36 months.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，在 18 到 24 个月大时就可以可靠地诊断出自闭症，最晚 36 个月肯定可以。

sentences.en: But 18 to 24 months, that diagnosis is quite stable.
sentences.zh: 但在 18 到 24 个月时，诊断结果已经相当稳定了。

sentences.en: The average age of diagnosis, though, in the United States is closer to five years of age.
sentences.zh: 然而，美国目前的平均确诊年龄接近 5 岁。

sentences.en: And even higher for families of color or individuals who may not have the resources to, you know, be able to obtain a diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 对于有色人种家庭或缺乏资源获取诊断的个人来说，这个年龄甚至更高。

sentences.en: So it takes many more visits to the doctor, for example, for a black child to receive a diagnosis than it does for a white child.
sentences.zh: 例如，黑人儿童获得诊断所需的就诊次数比白人儿童要多得多。

sentences.en: So we know we can diagnose by 18 to 24 months.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道 18 到 24 个月就能诊断。

sentences.en: We're obviously not doing a good enough job because the average age is much higher.
sentences.zh: 显然我们做得还不够好，因为平均年龄要高得多。

sentences.en: And by the way, the other thing that contributes to delay in diagnosis is being a girl.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，导致诊断延迟的另一个因素是性别为女性。

sentences.en: Because girls, we are just learning more about autism in girls and finding that the expression of the autism traits is somewhat different.
sentences.zh: 因为我们对女孩自闭症的了解还在增加，发现自闭症特征在女孩身上的表现有所不同。

sentences.en: So as you know, in neurotypical individuals, females tend to be a bit better at social interaction and picking up on social cues.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，在神经典型个体中，女性在社交互动和捕捉社交线索方面往往表现得更好。

sentences.en: There's been studies that have shown that, and this is true in autism as well.
sentences.zh: 已有研究表明了这一点，这在自闭症中也是如此。

sentences.en: So you may see better eye contact and therefore many girls are missed.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会看到更好的眼神交流，因此许多女孩被漏诊了。

sentences.en: The other thing that contributes to missing children is when autism is combined with a psychiatric condition.
sentences.zh: 导致漏诊的另一个因素是当自闭症合并其他精神疾病时。

sentences.en: So we know that, for example, about 50% of individuals with autism also have ADHD.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，例如，约 50% 的自闭症患者也患有多动症。

sentences.en: And so what happens is that when a young child presents with both autism and ADHD,
sentences.zh: 所以发生的情况是，当一个幼儿同时表现出自闭症和多动症时，

sentences.en: the ADHD symptoms tend to get more attention because ADHD is often associated with what we call externalizing behaviors.
sentences.zh: 多动症症状往往会受到更多关注，因为多动症通常与我们所说的“外化行为”相关。

sentences.en: These are things like, you know, you can't sit in your seat, you might be interrupting, you can't finish things, you might be, you know, blurting out.
sentences.zh: 这些行为包括：坐不住、插话、无法完成任务、脱口而出等。

sentences.en: And those behaviors are very disruptive and they tend to catch our attention more.
sentences.zh: 这些行为具有很强的破坏性，往往更容易引起我们的注意。

sentences.en: And we call this diagnostic overshadowing when a person has two conditions and one is kind of more obvious.
sentences.zh: 当一个人同时患有两种疾病，而其中一种更为明显时，我们称之为诊断掩盖。

sentences.en: That diagnosis tends to get, you know, the label for the child and then the other one is missed.
sentences.zh: 这种诊断往往会成为孩子的主要标签，而另一种疾病则被忽略了。

sentences.en: So when children have both autism and ADHD, they tend to be diagnosed at a much higher age.
sentences.zh: 因此，当孩子同时患有自闭症和多动症时，他们往往在年龄较大时才被确诊。

sentences.en: So, but I think the second question is, you know, when do the early behaviors or early signs of autism actually begin to emerge?
sentences.zh: 但我认为第二个问题是，自闭症的早期行为或早期迹象究竟何时开始显现？

sentences.en: And how early might we be able to detect autism?
sentences.zh: 我们可能在多早的阶段检测出自闭症？

sentences.en: So there's a lot of work going on and we've been doing some of this work in our lab as well, trying to identify autism in babies.
sentences.zh: 目前有很多相关研究，我们实验室也一直在进行这方面的工作，试图在婴儿期识别出自闭症。

sentences.en: Because there's been many studies now that, and some of this work was done by our team where we looked at home videos of infants who then were later diagnosed of autism.
sentences.zh: 因为现在已经有很多研究，其中一些是我们团队完成的，我们观察了后来被诊断为自闭症的婴儿的家庭录像。

sentences.en: But there's been many studies that have shown that between about 6 and 12 months of age, that the signs of autism begin to emerge in the majority of infants.
sentences.zh: 许多研究表明，在婴儿 6 到 12 个月大时，大多数婴儿就开始出现自闭症的迹象。

sentences.en: And those signs, and those signs could be the lack of communicative babbling.
sentences.zh: 这些迹象可能包括缺乏交流性的咿呀学语。

sentences.en: So we know, you know, during that period, babies tend to use consonant vowel sounds, you know, mama, baba, and they engage in this sort of back and forth with their parents.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，在此期间，婴儿通常会发出辅音和元音的声音，比如“妈妈”、“爸爸”，并与父母进行这种互动。

sentences.en: That is often absent or much delayed, the use of gestures.
sentences.zh: 而手势的使用往往缺失或严重滞后。

sentences.en: So we know that during that period, babies begin to start to use simple gestures such as bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，在此期间，婴儿开始使用简单的手势，比如挥手再见。

sentences.en: They also develop what is called joint attention, which is a set of gestures where the baby is drawing the parent's attention to something.
sentences.zh: 他们还会发展出所谓的“共同注意”，这是一系列手势，婴儿通过这些手势引起父母对某物的注意。

sentences.en: And they could do that, for example, by pointing at something to show them something.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们可以通过指着某样东西来向父母展示。

sentences.en: Or they might be interested if someone else points, they would follow that point and notice what others are doing.
sentences.zh: 或者，如果别人指着某样东西，他们会感兴趣，跟随那个指向并注意到别人在做什么。

sentences.en: That's why we call it shared or joint attention.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们称之为共享或共同注意的原因。

sentences.en: And those behaviors are quite diagnostic.
sentences.zh: 这些行为具有很强的诊断意义。

sentences.en: And so we see this lack of pointing, particularly to show.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们观察到缺乏指向行为，特别是缺乏展示性的指向。

sentences.en: Another sign could be some lack of interest in engaging with people as compared to objects.
sentences.zh: 另一个迹象可能是与物体相比，对与人互动缺乏兴趣。

sentences.en: So this baby may be very interested in objects and features of the non-social environment,
sentences.zh: 这个婴儿可能对物体和非社会环境的特征非常感兴趣，

sentences.en: but may be making less eye contact and not playing those baby games that we often see like pat a cake.
sentences.zh: 但可能较少进行眼神交流，也不玩我们常见的那些婴儿游戏，比如拍手游戏。

sentences.en: And so those and even the sensory sensitivities have been noticed in these young babies.
sentences.zh: 这些迹象，甚至包括感官敏感性，在这些年幼的婴儿身上都已被注意到。

sentences.en: So we should be able to pick up on autism during the infant period.
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该能够在婴儿期就发现自闭症。

sentences.en: And we're working on a lot of different ways that we may be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们正在研究多种可能实现这一目标的方法。

sentences.en: Some of those are ways of measuring behaviors.
sentences.zh: 其中一些是测量行为的方法。

sentences.en: Other ways are trying to see whether we could detect early changes in the way the brain is working and functioning.
sentences.zh: 其他方法则试图观察我们是否能检测到大脑工作和功能上的早期变化。

sentences.en: And I'm happy to talk about those.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意谈谈这些方法。

sentences.en: But there's a lot of work on looking at these brain-based, what are called biomarkers,
sentences.zh: 目前有很多关于这些基于大脑的所谓“生物标志物”的研究，

sentences.en: to see whether we can detect these even before we might be able to diagnose the full syndrome, which would be not until, say, 16 to 18 or 24 months of age.
sentences.zh: 旨在观察我们是否能在诊断出完整综合征之前就检测到这些迹象，通常这要等到 16 到 18 个月甚至 24 个月大时。

sentences.en: Well, when you're looking for brain-based biomarkers in very young children, how do you do that in a lab?
sentences.zh: 那么，当你在实验室寻找幼儿大脑生物标志物时，你是怎么做的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, how do you take a baby that's six months old and do, you know, an fMRI, for example?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你如何给一个六个月大的婴儿做功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）？

sentences.en: You can hardly do that with adults sometimes.
sentences.zh: 有时候连成年人都很难配合。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Actually, babies are easier than adults.
sentences.zh: 事实上，婴儿比成年人更容易配合。

sentences.en: Yes, for us that do brain research, it's interesting that, you know, babies, they take naps and they, you know,
sentences.zh: 是的，对于我们这些做脑科学研究的人来说，有趣的是，婴儿会小睡，而且，

sentences.en: they are actually much easier than the hardest period in terms of some of these measures is the toddler period where they want to, you know, get up and wiggle around.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上比幼儿期更容易配合，因为幼儿期是这些测量中最困难的时期，他们总想站起来动来动去。

sentences.en: But there are lots of different ways of studying the brain in infants.
sentences.zh: 但研究婴儿大脑的方法有很多种。

sentences.en: And most of the studies to date have followed infants who have an older sibling with autism that's already been diagnosed because we know that when there's one child in the family that's been diagnosed,
sentences.zh: 迄今为止，大多数研究都跟踪了那些有已确诊自闭症哥哥或姐姐的婴儿，因为我们知道，如果家里有一个孩子被确诊，

sentences.en: that the probability that the second child will have autism is about one in five.
sentences.zh: 那么第二个孩子患自闭症的概率大约是五分之一。

sentences.en: So that is a much higher rate.
sentences.zh: 所以这个比例要高得多。

sentences.en: And so by following these, what are called high likelihood infants prospectively, and then taking brain measures and behavior measures during infants, infancy,
sentences.zh: 通过前瞻性地跟踪这些所谓的“高可能性婴儿”，并在婴儿期进行大脑和行为测量，

sentences.en: we can then follow them longitudinally.
sentences.zh: 我们可以对他们进行纵向跟踪。

sentences.en: And then when that one in five is diagnosed with autism, we can look backwards and say, oh, well, what was different about their brain when we made those early measures?
sentences.zh: 当那五分之一的孩子被诊断出患有自闭症时，我们可以回顾过去，看看我们在早期测量时他们的大脑有什么不同。

sentences.en: So that's the way that the studies are mostly done.
sentences.zh: 这就是大多数研究进行的方式。

sentences.en: And in terms of the measures, there's been quite a bit of research looking at the development of the structure of the brain using MRI.
sentences.zh: 在测量方面，已经有不少研究利用核磁共振成像（MRI）观察大脑结构的发育。

sentences.en: So these are large collaborative studies occurring at multiple universities.
sentences.zh: 这些都是在多所大学进行的大型合作研究。

sentences.en: In fact, one of the biggest studies is led by my colleague, Joseph Piven, who's a psychiatrist down the road at UNC, Chapel Hill, because I'm at Duke, not very close by.
sentences.zh: 事实上，其中一项最大的研究是由我的同事 Joseph Piven 领导的，他是北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校的精神病学家，因为我在杜克大学，离得不太近。

sentences.en: And so he, for the last several years, has been following very large samples of high risk infants or high likelihood infants,
sentences.zh: 过去几年里，他一直跟踪着非常大样本的高风险或高可能性婴儿，

sentences.en: and then doing repeat MRIs to watch how the brain develops.
sentences.zh: 并进行重复的核磁共振扫描，以观察大脑是如何发育的。

sentences.en: And what he's found, he and his team, is that between six and 12 months of age, that the white matter of the brain,
sentences.zh: 他和他的团队发现，在 6 到 12 个月大时，大脑的白质，

sentences.en: so this is the part of the brain that helps different parts of the brain communicate with each other.
sentences.zh: 也就是大脑中帮助不同区域相互交流的部分，

sentences.en: So this is the myelin that goes around the connections of the brain that makes it more efficient in terms of the ability to communicate between two brain regions.
sentences.zh: 这是包裹在大脑连接周围的髓鞘，它提高了大脑两个区域之间交流的效率。

sentences.en: And what they found is that there's differences in the development of this white matter that can be seen by six to 12 months of age.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，白质的发育存在差异，在 6 到 12 个月大时就能观察到。

sentences.en: And essentially, what people are finding is that autism is a condition that affects the neural connectivity across different regions of the brain,
sentences.zh: 本质上，人们发现自闭症是一种影响大脑不同区域之间神经连接的疾病，

sentences.en: and these white matter fiber tracks.
sentences.zh: 以及这些白质纤维束。

sentences.en: And if you think about the behaviors that are affected by autism, which mostly is around social interaction and communication,
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑到受自闭症影响的行为，主要是社交互动和沟通，

sentences.en: those behaviors require the precise coordination across multiple brain regions.
sentences.zh: 这些行为需要多个大脑区域之间的精确协调。

sentences.en: So think about, for example, if you're involved in, say, you're watching their facial gestures, you're listening to the sound of their voice,
sentences.zh: 比如，当你参与对话时，你在观察对方的面部表情，倾听对方的声音，

sentences.en: you're anticipating the timing of the back and forth of the conversation, you're using your motor cortex to say words, for example.
sentences.zh: 你在预判对话往来的时机，你在使用运动皮层来说话，等等。

sentences.en: So even something like a conversation requires the frontal lobe, the visual cortex, the speech areas and auditory cortex, the motor cortex,
sentences.zh: 所以，即使是像对话这样简单的事情，也需要额叶、视觉皮层、语言区、听觉皮层和运动皮层的参与，

sentences.en: and these all have to be functioning in precise coordination.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都必须在精确的协调下运作。

sentences.en: And so we do think that autism affects the ability of the ability of the different brain regions to be coordinated in a way to allow us to engage in these very complex behaviors.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们确实认为自闭症影响了大脑不同区域协调运作的能力，从而影响了我们进行这些复杂行为的能力。

sentences.en: Now, I do want to take the opportunity here, though, to stress that autism also is associated with many positive traits, skills, and talents.
sentences.zh: 不过，我想借此机会强调，自闭症也与许多积极的特质、技能和天赋有关。

sentences.en: And that it's very likely that the sort of sacrifice of the ability to do some of these behaviors that are important, obviously, social interaction and communication.
sentences.zh: 虽然在某些重要行为（显然是社交互动和沟通）上可能存在能力缺失，

sentences.en: But it also offers the opportunity to be able to really view the world in a very different and unique way and to have very important and special talents.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也提供了一个以独特方式观察世界的机会，并可能带来非常重要和特殊的天赋。

sentences.en: And it probably has to do with the fact that there's probably large areas of the brain that are now able to be used for other things,
sentences.zh: 这可能与大脑中有大片区域现在能够被用于其他事情有关，

sentences.en: whether it's mathematics or music or art or physics.
sentences.zh: 无论是数学、音乐、艺术还是物理。

sentences.en: You know, so, you know, it's important to really think about autism as a brain difference that then comes with challenges, to be sure,
sentences.zh: 所以，将自闭症视为一种大脑差异是很重要的，它确实伴随着挑战，

sentences.en: but also with many very important and special strengths and talents as well.
sentences.zh: 但也伴随着许多非常重要和特殊的优势与天赋。

sentences.en: Now,
sentences.zh: 那么，

sentences.en: you published a study in February that found that an artificial intelligence algorithm could detect autism risk by screening infants' medical records right from the first month of life.
sentences.zh: 你在二月份发表了一项研究，发现人工智能算法可以通过筛查婴儿从出生第一个月起的医疗记录来检测自闭症风险。

sentences.en: That's pretty incredible.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: How does that work?
sentences.zh: 它是如何工作的？

sentences.en: So, we have been, we were awarded a grant from the National Institutes of Health that challenged us to come up with ways of screening for autism in babies.
sentences.zh: 我们获得了美国国立卫生研究院的一笔拨款，挑战我们提出筛查婴儿自闭症的方法。

sentences.en: Because, as I said before, it's clear that autism starts in infancy and we want to begin, you know, intervention services and support as early as possible.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我之前所说，很明显自闭症始于婴儿期，我们希望尽早开始干预服务和支持。

sentences.en: And so, we actually have been attacking this two ways.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们实际上一直在从两个方面入手。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 首先，

sentences.en: one is to gather information about the baby's healthcare record to see if there are clues in terms of how the infant is utilizing the healthcare system that might indicate that that baby would be more likely to have a later diagnosis of autism.
sentences.zh: 一是收集婴儿的医疗保健记录信息，看看婴儿利用医疗系统的方式中是否存在线索，可能预示着该婴儿未来更有可能被诊断为自闭症。

sentences.en: And the reason why we thought this might work is because autism is associated with quite a few medical conditions.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这可行，是因为自闭症与许多医疗状况有关。

sentences.en: So, people think about autism as a behavioral health condition, and it is, but it's also a physical health condition.
sentences.zh: 人们认为自闭症是一种行为健康状况，确实如此，但它也是一种身体健康状况。

sentences.en: So, for example, many people diagnosed with autism also have difficulties with the GI system.
sentences.zh: 例如，许多被诊断为自闭症的人也有胃肠道系统的问题。

sentences.en: So, in babies, this could be reflux, it could be diarrhea, constipation, other GI-related conditions.
sentences.zh: 在婴儿身上，这可能是反流、腹泻、便秘或其他胃肠道相关疾病。

sentences.en: And actually, in our studies, we are finding that these start very early, within the first three months of life.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在我们的研究中，我们发现这些问题在出生后的前三个月就开始了。

sentences.en: So, this is happening before we even start to see changes in behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以，这甚至在我们开始看到行为变化之前就已经发生了。

sentences.en: A second one is differences in the way the motor system is developed.
sentences.zh: 第二个方面是运动系统发育的差异。

sentences.en: So, we find that even during the first year of life,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，即使在出生后的第一年，

sentences.en: that babies who are going to go on to have a diagnosis of autism are visiting the physical therapist for difficulties in their motor development that are affected in the first year.
sentences.zh: 那些后来被诊断为自闭症的婴儿，因为在第一年就受到影响的运动发育困难，而正在看物理治疗师。

sentences.en: We also see higher rates of sleep disruptions, trouble establishing a circadian rhythm.
sentences.zh: 我们也观察到更高比例的睡眠障碍，以及难以建立昼夜节律。

sentences.en: And, in fact, there's been research that shows that some of the genetic genes that are responsible for regulating our circadian rhythm may contribute to autism.
sentences.zh: 事实上，已有研究表明，一些负责调节我们昼夜节律的基因可能与自闭症有关。

sentences.en: So, there are other conditions as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，还有其他一些情况。

sentences.en: But what we found was that if we can study how the parent is bringing their baby to receive these medical services in the first year of life,
sentences.zh: 但我们发现，如果我们能研究父母在第一年带婴儿接受这些医疗服务的方式，

sentences.en: that we can do a pretty good job of predicting, even in the first month, that this baby will have a higher likelihood of a diagnosis of autism.
sentences.zh: 我们就能很好地预测，即使在第一个月，这个婴儿患自闭症的可能性也会更高。

sentences.en: And the idea here is that if, you know, there's no way that a pediatrician could be, well,
sentences.zh: 这里的想法是，儿科医生不可能，嗯，

sentences.en: it would be very difficult for the pediatrician to have to look through and try to understand all of these patterns of healthcare utilization when the pediatrician, say,
sentences.zh: 儿科医生很难在给婴儿做健康检查时，去查看并理解所有这些医疗利用模式。

sentences.en: seeing the baby for a well-child visit.
sentences.zh: 所以，但计算机可以做到这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: So, but the computer can do this, right?
sentences.zh: 我们可以让计算机收集所有这些与健康相关的数据。

sentences.en: So, we can have the computer gathering all of this health-related data.
sentences.zh: 它可以是所有的诊断代码、所有类型的就诊、所有的药物、所有的程序，

sentences.en: It could be all the diagnostic codes, all the types of visits, all the medications, all the procedures,
sentences.zh: 然后利用人工智能或机器学习将所有这些数据组合成一个算法，从而预测特定的诊断，在本例中就是自闭症。

sentences.en: and then use artificial intelligence or machine learning to combine all of these data into an algorithm that then is predictive of a particular diagnosis, in this case, autism.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，我们也一直在研究多动症，发现这两者是可以区分的。

sentences.en: And we've been looking at the same thing for ADHD, by the way, and we find that these can be distinguished.
sentences.zh: 例如，一个后来被诊断为自闭症的婴儿，在一岁前去急诊室的可能性要大得多。

sentences.en: So, for example, a baby who is going to have a later diagnosis of autism is going to be much more likely to have visited the emergency room by age one.
sentences.zh: 这可能再次与冲动行为、冒险行为有关，或者其他可能导致事故的事情，最终导致去急诊室，对吧？

sentences.en: And this may have to do, again, with that impulsive behavior, risk-taking, you know, other things that might lead to accidents, right, that would end up in an emergency room.
sentences.zh: 所以，那里有大量的信息，可以，嗯，

sentences.en: So, you know, there's just a lot of information there that then can, you know,
sentences.zh: 帮助我们提醒儿科医生，他们需要特别关注这个婴儿，并密切监测其发育情况。

sentences.en: help us to let the pediatrician know that they need to be paying special attention to this baby and monitoring the baby's development very closely.
sentences.zh: 这些信息可以与所谓的“临床决策支持”相结合。

sentences.en: And this information can be combined with what is called clinical decision support.
sentences.zh: 这是目前医疗保健领域一个非常活跃的领域，儿科医生和其他医疗提供者会获得关于该患者是否，嗯，

sentences.en: So, this is a very active field now in healthcare where pediatricians and other providers are provided with information about whether this patient, you know,
sentences.zh: 患某种疾病的可能性更高的信息。

sentences.en: is a higher likelihood of developing, you know, a condition.
sentences.zh: 这可能是心脏相关疾病，在本例中是自闭症，然后还会为医生提供建议，他们应该怎么做？

sentences.en: It could be a heart-related condition, in this case, autism, and then also providing the physician with, well, what should they do about it?
sentences.zh: 所以，通过计算机给医生建议，比如，这可能意味着你需要进行转诊，或者根据年龄，

sentences.en: So, giving the physician through the computer advice about, okay, this means that, you know, you may want to make a referral for such and such, or depending on the age,
sentences.zh: 你可能确实需要转诊进行诊断评估。

sentences.en: you may actually want to refer for a diagnostic evaluation.
sentences.zh: 但这里有一些你可以跟踪这个婴儿并进行筛查的方法，看看行为是否正在显现。

sentences.en: But, you know, here's ways that you can follow this baby and screen, you know, to see if the behaviors are merging.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种方法。

sentences.en: So, that was one approach.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，这项工作是由我的同事 Matthew Engelhardt 领导的，他既是医生也是生物统计学家。

sentences.en: And by the way, that work was led by my colleague, Matthew Engelhardt, who is both a physician and a biostatistician.
sentences.zh: 所以他结合了医学和数据科学来完成这项非常了不起的工作。

sentences.en: So, he combines both medicine and data science to do this really phenomenal work.
sentences.zh: 我们现在已经获得了更多的资金来继续扩展这项工作。

sentences.en: And we're now, we've received more funding to continue to expand upon this work.
sentences.zh: 我们使用的第二种方法是利用计算机来测量那些早期的行为迹象。

sentences.en: And then the second approach that we've been using is to use the computer to measure those early behavioral signs.
sentences.zh: 这项工作最初是为了改进我们筛查自闭症的方法。

sentences.en: So, this work began to try to improve our ways of screening for autism.
sentences.zh: 目前，美国儿科学会建议所有幼儿在 18 个月和 24 个月的检查中接受普遍的自闭症筛查。

sentences.en: So, currently, the American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that all toddlers be screened universally for autism at their 18- and 24-month visit.
sentences.zh: 请记住，那是我们可以做出诊断的年龄。

sentences.en: And remember, that's the age where we can make a diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 所以，这很好，因为你可以在那个年龄进行诊断评估，

sentences.en: So, you know, it's good in terms of you can have, you know, a diagnostic evaluation at that age,
sentences.zh: 但不好的一点是，他们通常接受了筛查，然后需要时间进行转诊。

sentences.en: but it's not so good in the sense that what happens is that they often get screened and then it takes time to make the referral.
sentences.zh: 然后他们进入诊断等待名单，通常等待名单很长。

sentences.en: Then they get on a waiting list for a diagnosis and there's often a long waiting liSt.
sentences.zh: 在得到诊断后，他们又进入另一个等待名单以获得干预。

sentences.en: And then after they get the diagnosis, they're on another waiting list to get the intervention.
sentences.zh: 所以，在干预开始前可能需要一年或更长时间。

sentences.en: So, you know, there can be a year or before intervention begins.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在看到的是 36 个月甚至 48 个月大。

sentences.en: So, now we're looking at 36, you know, or even, you know, 48 months of age.
sentences.zh: 我们真的想把所有这些时间提前。

sentences.en: So, we really want to shift all of that earlier.
sentences.zh: 但这种筛查方法存在问题。

sentences.en: But there was problems with this screening approach.
sentences.zh: 通常，18 个月和 24 个月时的筛查是通过家长问卷进行的。

sentences.en: So, typically, how this is done at 18- and 24-months is with a parent questionnaire.
sentences.zh: 这是一个简单的问卷，普遍发放，例如在杜克大学的初级保健中，

sentences.en: And it's a simple questionnaire given universally, for example, here at Duke in primary care,
sentences.zh: 你问家长 20 个问题，这些问题与我之前提到的那些行为有关。

sentences.en: where you ask the parents about 20 questions that have to do with those behaviors that I mentioned earlier.
sentences.zh: 你的孩子会指东西吗？他们会用词吗？他们对游戏感兴趣吗？他们会模仿你吗？

sentences.en: Is your child pointing, are they using words, are they interested in games, do they imitate you?
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的问题。

sentences.en: So, questions like that.
sentences.zh: 然后根据家长回答的“是”或“否”的数量，他们会被认为患自闭症的可能性更高。

sentences.en: And then depending on, you know, how many yeses or noes in this case that the parent says, then they would be considered to have a higher likelihood of autism.
sentences.zh: 希望医疗提供者能进行转诊。

sentences.en: And hopefully, the provider would make a referral.
sentences.zh: 有趣的一个发现是，大多数儿科医生仍然不进行转诊。

sentences.en: Now, one of the interesting findings is that most pediatricians still don't make a referral.
sentences.zh: 大约 60% 的情况下，即使家长问卷筛查结果呈阳性，他们也不会进行转诊。

sentences.en: About 60% of the time, they, even with a positive screen on a parent questionnaire, they don't make a referral.
sentences.zh: 他们采取“观望”的态度。

sentences.en: They take a wait-and-see approach.
sentences.zh: 部分原因与他们对解读信息缺乏信心有关。

sentences.en: And part of it has to do with just their lack of confidence in interpreting the information.
sentences.zh: 部分原因可能与寻找服务困难有关，以及不愿让家长踏上一段可能非常令人沮丧且昂贵的旅程。

sentences.en: And part of it may have to do with the difficulty in finding services and some reluctance to, you know, send the parent on a journey that can be very frustrating and costly.
sentences.zh: 或者告诉家长他们认为孩子在谱系上，结果可能是错的，对吧？

sentences.en: Or telling the parent that they think that the child is on the spectrum and then maybe being wrong, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们可能是错的。

sentences.en: I mean, they could be.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这也是一个重要的点，因为最常见的问卷被称为“幼儿自闭症改良检查表”或 MCHAT。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think that's an important point, too, because so the most common questionnaire is called the Modified Checklist for Autism and Toddlers or the MCHAT.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，我们很高兴有 MCHAT，也很高兴儿科医生使用它。

sentences.en: And by the way, we are so happy we have the MCHAT and we are so happy that pediatricians use it.
sentences.zh: 所以我绝不是想说我们应该阻止使用 MCHAT。

sentences.en: So I'm not in any way wanting to say we should discourage use of the MCHAT.
sentences.zh: 但如果孩子被转诊，他们大约有 50% 的机会被诊断为自闭症。

sentences.en: But if the child is referred, you know, they will have about a 50-50 chance of having a diagnosis of autism.
sentences.zh: 这意味着会有一些假阳性，许多人等待诊断却并不需要，这增加了那些漫长的等待名单。

sentences.en: So that does mean that there will be some, you know, false positives, many people waiting to get a diagnosis that don't need to and adding to those long wait lists.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为所有这些都导致了转诊的犹豫。

sentences.en: So all of that, I think, is contributing to this reluctance to make a referral.
sentences.zh: 但还有其他问题，或者说也存在其他问题。

sentences.en: But there were other problems, or there are other problems as well.
sentences.zh: MCHAT 在有色人种家庭中的效果并不理想。

sentences.en: So the MCHAT does not work as well with families of color.
sentences.zh: MCHAT 在有色人种家庭中的效果并不理想。

sentences.en: So we don't completely understand it,
sentences.zh: 虽然我们还没有完全理解它，

sentences.en: but there are reasons why from different cultures that have different attitudes around providing information or how they interpret information.
sentences.zh: 但不同文化背景下，人们在提供信息或解读信息方面的态度各异，这其中是有原因的。

sentences.en: The other thing is that it does require literacy and understanding of child development.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，这需要一定的文化素养和对儿童发展的理解。

sentences.en: And, you know, many parents may not have those skills.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，许多父母可能并不具备这些技能。

sentences.en: And so for those reasons, when it's used in real-world settings like primary care, it's really not performing as well as it should.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于这些原因，当它在初级保健等现实环境中应用时，效果确实不如预期。

sentences.en: It also is not as good at picking up autism in girls.
sentences.zh: 它在识别女孩自闭症方面的表现也不够好。

sentences.en: So what we wanted to do was to develop a methodology where we could directly observe the child's behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想做的是开发一种方法，可以直接观察孩子的行为。

sentences.en: Because we know, I mean, autism is a behavioral diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 因为我们知道，自闭症是一种行为诊断。

sentences.en: So we should be able to directly observe what the child is doing and try to pick up on the behavioral signs.
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该能够直接观察孩子在做什么，并尝试捕捉到行为迹象。

sentences.en: And some people have tried to have the pediatrician do this, but honestly, they don't have the time.
sentences.zh: 有些人尝试让儿科医生来做这件事，但老实说，他们没有时间。

sentences.en: And also, they have so many things that they're screening for and concerned about.
sentences.zh: 而且，他们需要筛查和关注的事情太多了。

sentences.en: They don't have a time to do a diagnostic assessment as part of their well-child 15-minute often visit.
sentences.zh: 在他们通常 15 分钟的儿童健康检查中，他们没有时间进行诊断评估。

sentences.en: So we decided to try to use a technique called computer vision analysis, which is a way of the computer with a computer, using a computer to measure behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以我们决定尝试使用一种称为计算机视觉分析的技术，这是一种利用计算机来测量行为的方法。

sentences.en: And the way this works is we designed an app, and this can be downloaded on a smartphone or a tablet.
sentences.zh: 它的工作原理是我们设计了一个应用程序，可以下载到智能手机或平板电脑上。

sentences.en: And the app displays a set of short movies.
sentences.zh: 该应用程序会播放一系列短片。

sentences.en: And these movies were strategically designed by our team to elicit autism-related behaviors.
sentences.zh: 这些短片是由我们的团队精心设计的，旨在诱发与自闭症相关的行为。

sentences.en: So to elicit facial expressions and vocalizations, to assess, to be able to see whether the baby is more interested in looking at objects versus people.
sentences.zh: 比如诱发面部表情和发声，以评估并观察婴儿是对物体更感兴趣，还是对人更感兴趣。

sentences.en: And so these, again, were very carefully designed.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些短片再次强调，是经过非常仔细设计的。

sentences.en: So the baby watches these brief movies.
sentences.zh: 婴儿观看这些简短的视频。

sentences.en: It's all done within less than 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 整个过程在不到 10 分钟内完成。

sentences.en: And the camera that's in the device, whether it's a smartphone or a tablet, is recording the baby's responses.
sentences.zh: 设备（无论是智能手机还是平板电脑）中的摄像头会记录下婴儿的反应。

sentences.en: Then the engineering team uses computer vision to automatically code a wide range of behaviors.
sentences.zh: 然后工程团队利用计算机视觉自动编码各种行为。

sentences.en: So a computer can code facial expressions, vocalizations, head turns, body movements.
sentences.zh: 计算机可以对表情、发声、转头、身体动作进行编码。

sentences.en: It can do all of this.
sentences.zh: 它能做到这一切。

sentences.en: And what's really amazing is it can do it better than a human.
sentences.zh: 真正令人惊叹的是，它做得比人类更好。

sentences.en: And I truly believe this.
sentences.zh: 我对此深信不疑。

sentences.en: And I, of course, have been observing behavior as a psychologist my entire career and coding a lot of behavior.
sentences.zh: 当然，作为一名心理学家，我的整个职业生涯都在观察行为并对大量行为进行编码。

sentences.en: But I'll give you an example.
sentences.zh: 但我给你举个例子。

sentences.en: So one of the early signs is not orienting when your name is called.
sentences.zh: 早期迹象之一是叫名字时没有反应。

sentences.en: So while the baby is watching the movies, someone behind them actually calls their name.
sentences.zh: 当婴儿观看视频时，身后有人会叫他们的名字。

sentences.en: And, you know, the baby will typically turn their head.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，婴儿会转过头来。

sentences.en: And a computer can precisely measure that.
sentences.zh: 而计算机可以精确地测量这一点。

sentences.en: And what we found was that, indeed, that babies who then later had a diagnosis of autism did not turn their head as frequently.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，后来被诊断为自闭症的婴儿确实转头频率较低。

sentences.en: But some of them did turn their head.
sentences.zh: 但其中一些确实转头了。

sentences.en: And what we found was that when they turned their head, they did it a second delayed compared to the neurotypical babies.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当他们转头时，与神经发育正常的婴儿相比，他们延迟了一秒。

sentences.en: And there's no way a clinician could have seen that.
sentences.zh: 临床医生是不可能观察到这一点的。

sentences.en: So the clinician would have said the baby doesn't have that sign.
sentences.zh: 所以临床医生会说这个婴儿没有那个迹象。

sentences.en: But the computer was able to do this at a much higher resolution.
sentences.zh: 但计算机能够以更高的分辨率做到这一点。

sentences.en: So we are now we have now validated this in the 18 to 24 month age.
sentences.zh: 我们现在已经在 18 到 24 个月大的年龄段验证了这一点。

sentences.en: And we also are just completed a study where we've shown that this can be done at home.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚完成了一项研究，证明这可以在家里完成。

sentences.en: So parents can download the app at home and those data can be sent to the pediatrician ahead of time, right before the visit,
sentences.zh: 父母可以在家里下载该应用程序，数据可以在就诊前提前发送给儿科医生，

sentences.en: so that they have assessments of the child behaviors that could also be done over time to track behavioral development.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就能获得孩子行为的评估结果，这些评估也可以随着时间的推移进行，以跟踪行为发展。

sentences.en: And the study we're doing now is starting at six months of age and then following babies longitudinally.
sentences.zh: 我们目前正在进行的研究从六个月大开始，然后对婴儿进行纵向跟踪。

sentences.en: And they were repeating the app over time.
sentences.zh: 他们会随着时间的推移重复使用该应用程序。

sentences.en: And they will see whether this can be used to eventually pick up on signs in, you know, in babies who then will have a diagnosis of autism.
sentences.zh: 我们将观察这是否最终能用于识别那些后来被诊断为自闭症的婴儿的迹象。

sentences.en: So I think it's, you know, I started my career by trying to understand autism in infants by looking at home videotapes that parents had gathered.
sentences.zh: 我认为，我职业生涯的开始就是通过观看父母收集的家庭录像带，试图了解婴儿的自闭症。

sentences.en: And now I'm using artificial intelligence and computer science to measure these on an app that's on a smartphone.
sentences.zh: 而现在，我正在利用人工智能和计算机科学，通过智能手机上的应用程序来测量这些行为。

sentences.en: So I would have never imagined that.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未想象过这一点。

sentences.en: Technology just can't keep up with it.
sentences.zh: 技术的发展速度简直让人跟不上。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: So let me ask you one wrap-up question, which has to do with why the early diagnosis is important.
sentences.zh: 让我问你最后一个总结性问题，这与为什么早期诊断很重要有关。

sentences.en: And obviously, we've been talking about the concept of interventions without actually describing them.
sentences.zh: 显然，我们一直在谈论干预的概念，但没有具体描述它们。

sentences.en: But if a parent gets the diagnosis early enough, what is it that the parent should then do to help the child?
sentences.zh: 但如果父母足够早地得到诊断，他们应该做些什么来帮助孩子呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you for that question, because that is, you know, really the crux of the matter.
sentences.zh: 是的，谢谢你提出这个问题，因为这确实是问题的核心。

sentences.en: The reason why we want to detect autism early is to provide services and intervention.
sentences.zh: 我们想要早期发现自闭症的原因是为了提供服务和干预。

sentences.en: So I'll describe a type of intervention that is very commonly used now.
sentences.zh: 我将描述一种现在非常常用的干预类型。

sentences.en: These are a class of interventions called naturalistic developmental behavioral interventions.
sentences.zh: 这是一类被称为自然主义发展行为干预的干预措施。

sentences.en: They evolved out of traditional applied behavior analysis, which is a technique that has been used for many years as an intervention model.
sentences.zh: 它们是从传统的应用行为分析演变而来的，这是一种多年来一直被用作干预模型的技术。

sentences.en: This is sort of a newer version that is much more play-based, much more naturalistic.
sentences.zh: 这是一种较新的版本，更基于游戏，更自然。

sentences.en: We follow the infant or the toddler's lead and capitalize on their interests and preferences, which makes the therapy much more engaging, both for the child and the parent.
sentences.zh: 我们跟随婴儿或幼儿的引导，利用他们的兴趣和偏好，这使得治疗对孩子和父母都更具吸引力。

sentences.en: But essentially, these interventions use play and naturalistic interventions to facilitate the baby's, first of all, interest in other people.
sentences.zh: 但本质上，这些干预措施利用游戏和自然主义干预来促进婴儿首先对他人产生兴趣。

sentences.en: So to bring the baby's attention back to people, because remember, this infant or toddler is now much more interested in toys and the world of objects than people.
sentences.zh: 所以要让婴儿的注意力回到人身上，因为请记住，这个婴儿或幼儿现在对玩具和物体世界比对人更感兴趣。

sentences.en: But there are ways of using play and inserting yourself into the interests of the baby or the child where you become part of their world.
sentences.zh: 但有一些方法可以利用游戏，让自己融入婴儿或孩子的兴趣中，从而成为他们世界的一部分。

sentences.en: And then they will naturally start to be interested in you and looking at you.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会自然地开始对你感兴趣并注视你。

sentences.en: Once that happens, then we, again, use these techniques to teach the infant or the toddler how to use gestures,
sentences.zh: 一旦发生这种情况，我们再次使用这些技术来教婴儿或幼儿如何使用手势，

sentences.en: how to communicate through a set of strategies that can be taught to parents to use at home or delivered by a therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 如何通过一套可以教给父母在家中使用或由治疗师提供的策略进行交流。

sentences.en: And so these parent, what are called parent-mediated therapies, are ones where we work with the parent to learn these strategies that they can use during their everyday activities.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些所谓的父母介导疗法，是我们与父母合作，学习他们可以在日常活动中使用的策略。

sentences.en: So if you think about a neurotypical infant, they are, we don't sit them down and say,
sentences.zh: 如果你想到一个神经发育正常的婴儿，我们不会让他们坐下来，然后说，

sentences.en: I'm going to teach you now how to speak or I'm going to teach you how to recognize that this is a smile.
sentences.zh: 我现在要教你如何说话，或者我要教你如何识别这是一个微笑。

sentences.en: It happens during every interaction during the day is an opportunity for learning during mealtime and bath time at the park.
sentences.zh: 它发生在每一次互动中，每一天都是学习的机会，比如用餐时间、洗澡时间和在公园里。

sentences.en: And so similarly, these interventions that are taught to parents are ones where the parents can use these strategies just throughout their everyday activities.
sentences.zh: 同样，这些教给父母的干预措施，是父母可以在日常活动中使用的策略。

sentences.en: So we have a book, for example, it's called An Early Start for Your Child with Autism, and it is written for parents and it teaches them a wide range of strategies they can use.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们有一本书，叫《自闭症儿童的早期启动》，它是为父母写的，教给他们各种可以使用的策略。

sentences.en: And it has to do with things like, how do you position yourself?
sentences.zh: 它涉及一些事情，比如，你如何调整自己的位置？

sentences.en: For example, when you sit down to read a book with your baby or your child, you're not going to sit them on your lap, you know, where they're faced away from you.
sentences.zh: 例如，当你坐下来和你的婴儿或孩子读书时，你不会让他们坐在你的膝盖上，你知道，背对着你。

sentences.en: So you're going to sit them where they're faced forward to you.
sentences.zh: 所以你要让他们面对着你坐。

sentences.en: So you're going to have yourself in their zone of proximity and also in their spotlight, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 所以你要让自己处于他们的亲近区域，也可以说是处于他们的焦点中心。

sentences.en: Then you're going to learn how to kind of capitalize on the things that the baby is interested in to start to facilitate things like turn taking.
sentences.zh: 然后你要学习如何利用婴儿感兴趣的事情，开始促进轮流互动等事情。

sentences.en: You're going to do a lot of imitation of the baby's or the toddler's vocalizations and actions.
sentences.zh: 你要大量模仿婴儿或幼儿的发声和动作。

sentences.en: So we find that, let's say that this two-year-old is banging on something and not looking at you.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，假设这个两岁的孩子在敲打什么东西，而不看你。

sentences.en: If you have a drum two and you bang it the same time, that two-year-old with autism is going to start looking at you, playing with it,
sentences.zh: 如果你也有一个鼓，同时敲打它，那个患有自闭症的两岁孩子就会开始看着你，一起玩耍，

sentences.en: and pretty soon you're in a fun back-and-forth game where you're both, you know, playing the jumps together.
sentences.zh: 很快你们就会进入一个有趣的来回游戏，你们都在一起玩跳跃游戏。

sentences.en: And so these are relatively easy to learn.
sentences.zh: 所以这些相对容易学习。

sentences.en: Parents are very good at learning them.
sentences.zh: 父母非常擅长学习这些。

sentences.en: And they've been shown to really facilitate early social and communication development.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，它们确实能促进早期的社交和沟通发展。

sentences.en: So we're very excited about, you know, parents using these.
sentences.zh: 所以我们对父母使用这些方法感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And again, they can be delivered by therapists as well, and they can make a huge difference in children's outcomes.
sentences.zh: 同样，它们也可以由治疗师提供，并且可以对儿童的结果产生巨大的影响。

sentences.zh: 这真的非常有趣，我相信我们的听众从你的讲述中会学到很多。

sentences.en: So thank you.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你。

sentences.en: Oh, it's been my pleasure.
